shaders.name: Shaders: What a Surface Answers To
shaders.truth: A shader is a rule run for every pixel at once. It keeps no memory and has no body; what it answers to is light, position and time. The passage, the pillar hall and the basin are where the museum lets that show.
shaders.qfep_connection: The field of the noise sequence becomes a surface. Every pixel is computed from the same rule with different inputs, and nothing is kept between frames until a buffer gives the rule a past; the hall after this one gives the cell one. What a surface can answer to, and what carries the body that looks at it, are two constructions the sequence keeps apart.
shaders.formula: colour = f(position, light, time), for every pixel, at once
shaders.description: Six halls assembled from the Book of Shaders rooms and introduced through the architecture between rooms: a long passage where a rule runs for every pixel at once, a pillar hall where five materials answer light, a basin whose glass lid carries you over moving water, the floor of the tiling sequence returned as a per-pixel rule, five materials pushed past their intended range, and a rule given a memory through a buffer, which is where cellular automata begin.
learning_objectives: Say what a fragment shader receives (position, light, time) and what it cannot keep (a memory) or be (a body)
Read a shaping function as a policy for where value goes, and a gradient as never neutral
Distinguish a material that answers light (leather, latex, oil slick) from a mesh that merely has a colour
Stand on a basin lid over moving water and tell the surface you look at from the construction that carries you
Recognise the tiling sequence’s floor as a per-pixel fold of space rather than a set of copies
Explain why a buffer turns a rule for every pixel into a rule with a past, and carry that into cellular automata
content: Shader_01_Shaping: A rule for every pixel at once - arrive through the passage; y = f(x) as a policy for where light goes
Shader_11_QueerRubber: The pillar hall: what a surface answers to - five materials under three coloured lights, between the piers the museum keeps here
Shader_09_FBM: The basin: water without a memory - the pool’s glass lid carries you; the water on it is recomputed from the clock on every frame
Shader_05_Patterns: The floor returned - fract() folds space; bricks, Truchet and Voronoi as one function
Shader_12_PinkExtravaganza: Past the intended range - every uniform cranked past taste; the water on this floor refracts wrong on purpose
Shader_10_ReactionDiffusion: A rule given a memory - reaction-diffusion in a buffer; the same rule run again on what it drew, which is where the next sequence starts

deferred_reason.Shader_02_Colors: colour is sequence four’s; the hall stays on disk for the pattern-generation walk
deferred_reason.Shader_03_Shapes: kept for the pattern-generation walk; the six spine halls carry the argument
deferred_reason.Shader_07_Noise: noise is sequence eleven’s; FBM carries the field here
deferred_reason.Shader_08_CellularNoise: Voronoi appears inside the patterns hall
deferred_reason.Shader_Arch_Gallery: a 65-row gallery, not a hall of the walk
